title: Nanocrates: Inside-Out Scaffolds for Sample Protection from the Air-Water Interface During Cryo-EM Sample Preparation
content: The air-water interface (AWI) interaction is a well-known issue affecting macromolecules during cryo-EM sample preparation. Contact with the AWI can lead txo uneven sample distribution, preferred orientation, and damage to the molecules of interest. We are proposing a solution to AWI issues by encaging the target proteins within highly hydrophilic, structurally homogeneous, and stable protein-based "nanocrates". These nanocrates act as inside-out scaffolds, where the particles are protected within the lumen of another particle, rather than being presented on the outside. Such nanocrates can be reconstructed to high resolution with only a few thousand particles. The nanocrate densities can then be subtracted from the particle stacks, revealing the cargo (the protein of interest) in the remaining densities. Here, we provide proof of principle and describe the packaging, data acquisition, and reconstruction of apoferritin (ApoF) within MS2 cages.
